{{Quote|On Tatooine, each second of life is viewed as both a curse and a blessing. Throughout every waking moment, one is engaged in some battle for existence. To achieve any hope for survival in such a harsh, brutal place, one needs to become just as harsh and brutal.|Alkhara|<ref name="Outlander" />}}
'''Alkhara''' was a researcher from the [[Tatooine Bureau of Ethnicity and Socialization|Bureau of Ethnicity and Socialization]] on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] who lived in the [[600 BBY/Legends|sixth century]] [[Galactic Standard Calendar|BBY]] and became a notorious criminal. He was also the man who incited the centuries-long [[Blood/Legends|blood]] feud between the native [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Sand People]] and the [[Human/Legends|Human]] settlers of the [[Planet/Legends|world]]. In his years with the Bureau, Alkhara learned the language and traditions of the Sand People, filing reports in which he mused on the nature of their life on Tatooine. After he turned to crime, Alkhara joined with the Sand People to destroy a police garrison, then turned on his allies in a massacre. He and his band of thieves fled the retaliation of the Sand People and authorities to a [[B'omarr Order/Legends|B'omarr]] [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|monastery]], where they were welcomed in.

Alkhara made the monastery his headquarters, using it to defend against the Sand People and rob the local [[Moisture farmer/Legends|moisture farmers]]. He and his band expanded and improved the structure, adding dungeons, a tower, and roads. The monks ignored them for the most part, though they were grateful for many of the additions. After living in the monastery for over three decades, Alkhara was driven offworld by the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]], and eventually [[Death/Legends|died]]. However, the war he had triggered with the Sand People long outlived him. Centuries afterward, bandit groups under his name continued their own crimes against the settlers and battles against the natives, while the monastery he had made his home fell into a number of new hands, amongst them Jabba's.

==Biography==
{{Quote|Well, a long time ago, there was this bandit named Alkhara. Allied himself with the Sand People, and took out a police garrison. Problem is, he immediately turned on the Sand People that helped him and slaughtered them all.|[[Reelo Baruk]], to a spacer|<ref name="SWG:JPRB">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=general|Jabba's Palace : Reelo Baruk|Tatooine}}</ref>}}
In [[550 BBY]], Alkhara arrived on the planet [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].<ref name="SoT" /> Working in a [[Mining/Legends|mining]] colony for the [[Tatooine Bureau of Ethnicity and Socialization|Bureau of Ethnicity and Socialization]], Alkhara became familiar with the native [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Sand People]]. In the course of his studies, Alkhara ventured into the [[Jundland Wastes/Legends|Jundland Wastes]] and the ancient canyon the Sand People called [[Gafsa/Legends|Gafsa]], learning the [[Tusken/Legends|language]] and traditions of the natives. Alkhara came to conclude that having been born into a cruel world, the Sand People knew nothing but cruelty and lacked in benign emotions. He opined as such in one of his field reports filed with the Bureau.<ref name="Outlander" />

In time, Alkhara turned to crime, becoming a bandit, and his crimes became legendary.<ref name="ITW">''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars Trilogy]]''</ref> Alkhara allied himself and his band of thieves with the Sand People to eliminate a small law enforcement garrison near Tatooine's capital. He then turned on the Sand People themselves, massacring the entire group that had aided him on the [[Great Mesra Plateau/Legends|Great Mesra Plateau]].<ref name="ISWU" /><ref name="ITW" /><ref name="CorSec">{{SonyCite|url=players/guides.vm?id=80112|text=CorSec Database A-G|int=CorSec Database A-G}}</ref> Alkhara's actions triggered a feud between the Sand People and [[Human/Legends|Human]] settlers. Fleeing military retribution from the law and the Sand People, the bandit and his followers escaped to a [[B'omarr Order/Legends|B'omarr]] [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|monastery]]. There, they intended to lay siege to the citadel, but the gates were unlocked. The monks were unimpressed with the armed group, and, to Alkhara's surprise, one monk told the leader to make himself at home and stay as long as he liked.<ref name="SoT" /><ref name="ISWU" /> Unknown to Alkhara, other lawbreakers had used the monastery as a temporary refuge in the past&mdash;though none, until Alkhara, had occupied it for their own use&mdash;and the monks did not mind as the pirate and his band moved in.<ref name="SoT" /><ref name="ITW" />

With the monks few in number and absorbed in their own concerns, Alkhara was free to use the monastery as his headquarters.<ref name="ISWU" /> With the citadel serving as his stronghold against the Sand People,<ref name="Jabba">{{DB|location|jabbathehuttspalace|Jabba the Hutt's Palace}}</ref> the bandit preyed on the [[Moisture farmer/Legends|moisture farmers]] of Tatooine.<ref name="Darksaber">[[Darksaber (novel)|''Darksaber'']]</ref> Alkhara improved his hideout, augmenting its corridors while his followers fixed the living quarters and added a set of dungeons and underground chambers, to the monks' approval.<ref name="ISWU" /> He cut a road from the citadel to the [[Western Dune Sea/Legends|Western Dune Sea]] and [[Great Pit of Carkoon/Legends|Pit of Carkoon]]. Alkhara also added battlements to the building, and he renovated a [[Alkhara's tower|nine-story tower]] to which he gave his name. Alkhara lived in the monastery for thirty-four years, until he was driven off Tatooine by the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]].<ref name="ITW" />

Alkhara eventually died, but the feud he had started between the settlers and Sand People continued for centuries thereafter. In later years, his [[Alkhara Bandits|bandit group]] was reformed by Tatooinians who had been dislocated by the Sand People, fighting the natives while raiding villages and moisture farms for supplies.<ref name="CorSec" /> No outlanders ventured into Sand People territory for centuries, as well.<ref name="Outlander" /> The B'omarr monastery took on a number of new occupants in the ages after Alkhara's departure, all of them following the traditions of Alkhara's people by expanding and improving the structure in exchange; eventually, Jabba the Hutt would take it as his palace.<ref name="ISWU" />

==Personality and traits==
Fierce and with a reputation for cruelty that endured for centuries, Alkhara achieved notoriety in his career as a bandit, and his crimes became things of legend.<ref name="ITW" /><ref name="CorSec" /><ref name="SWE">''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> The man could break his alliances, turning on allies in a deadly fashion; however, he could also participate in mutually beneficial relationships, as with the B'omarr monks. While he was not adverse to fleeing danger, Alkhara was prepared for combat.<ref name="ISWU" />

In his time with the Bureau of Ethnology and Socialization, Alkhara came to his own understanding of Tatooine and its inhabitants. He saw the harshness of life on the world to breed, by necessity, harshness in its inhabitants. The only way he felt one could understand the Sand People was to live their lives; he believed they had been shaped in such a way that cruelty and wickedness were their way of life, and he doubted any gentler emotions lived within them.<ref name="Outlander" /> When he turned to his life of pirating, Alkhara was callous towards the Sand People.<ref name="SoT" />

==Behind the scenes==
Alkhara was given a brief mention as a prior owner of Jabba the Hutt's palace in the [[1995]] novel [[Darksaber (novel)|''Darksaber'']], by [[Kevin J. Anderson]]. Anderson would later expand on his backstory in his book ''[[The Illustrated Star Wars Universe]]'', which gave Alkhara the crucial role he has in the Sand People/Human conflict. The comic arc ''[[Star Wars: Outlander]]'' gave the character the only backstory he has in his time before becoming a criminal, and the only dialogue the character has ever had, as he has made no appearances in any works. The exact timeframe for Alkhara's life was left vague until ''[[Secrets of Tatooine]]''.
